newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU favors direct settlement with U.S. over Helms-Burton Act.
newsitem.headline: EU favors direct settlement with U.S. over Helms-Burton Act.

text.p: The European Union said Monday it would rather resolve differences with the United States over its anti-Cuba legislation directly with Washington rather than have the World Trade Organisation rule on the matter.
Diplomats said EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels expressed regret that recent talks with Washington over the Helms-Burton Act showed deep differences remain.
However, the EU foreign ministers expressed their willingness to "continue to seek an overall bilateral settlement and in that case to halt or suspend the panel procedure" at the WTO.

The act -- the culmination of years of U.S. policy aimed at isolating the Cuban government of Fidel Castro -- was passed last year to a chorus of indignation from European and other allies of the United States.

Among other things the law allows Americans to sue in U.S. courts any foreign companies and individuals deemed to have gained from investments in former American property confiscated by the Cuban government since the communist revolution in 1959.

Although this part of the legislation has twice been suspended by President Clinton, the EU is also opposed to another section that prohibits foreigners with links to companies investing in confiscated property from entering the United States.

Last week WTO chief Renato Ruggiero named a three-member panel to adjudicate the matter, but Washington said it would not cooperate and reserved its right to invoke a little-used "national security clause" in its defence.
